name: YouTube Music Premium
subcategory: music services and creator audio tools
tagline: Organize and stream user-owned audio without accessing YouTube's licensed catalog

pricing.notes: Typical US monthly Individual price; current package should be rechecked.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1 account; ad-supported listening; no numeric listening cap is publicly stated.

tiers.name: Individual
tiers.notes: A prepaid annual Individual option exists, but the exact current U.S. annual checkout total was not exposed on the public page checked.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 account; ad-supported listening; no numeric listening cap is publicly stated.
pricing.billingTerms: Individual is monthly or prepaid annual, but the exact current U.S. annual total is checkout-only; Family and Student are monthly. The annual plan is non-recurring, nonrefundable, cannot be paused and can be stacked up to 24 months.
pricing.hiddenCosts: App-store/Google Play billing can differ from direct web pricing; the prepaid annual plan has no prorated refund and cannot be paused.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For YouTube Music Premium, organize and stream user-owned audio without accessing YouTube's licensed catalog. The hard boundary is youtube catalog, videos, rights, recommendations, identity, and global delivery, plus licensed content, rights, and distribution network.
coreLoopDIY: Organize and stream legally owned or user-created audio, analyze local files, and provide a private playback workflow without accessing YouTube's licensed catalog.
whatYouLose: YouTube catalog, videos, rights, recommendations, identity, and global delivery
moatNotes: licensed content, rights, and distribution network
ongoingBurden: catalog licensing, royalties, identity, content delivery, moderation, recommendations, payouts, codecs, and rights disputes
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for YouTube Music Premium because the product is the catalog, rights chain, and distribution network; a player or processing tool is only the visible edge. The recurring cost buys catalog licensing, royalties, identity, content delivery, moderation, recommendations, payouts, codecs, and rights disputes, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Navidrome
priorArt.desc: Active open-source personal music server for legally owned libraries.

alternatives.name: Navidrome
alternatives.desc: Your music, your disk, your streaming server; the licensed catalogue is the part it cannot clone.

facts.install: Docker Compose or a prebuilt Windows/macOS/Linux binary; install ffmpeg
facts.dataFormat: Music remains as audio files in the configured music folder; users, playlists and indexed metadata live in Navidrome's application database under its data folder, with cache files beside it
facts.gapVsPaid: It cannot access YouTube Music's licensed songs, videos, remixes, live performances, uploads ecosystem, recommendations, or Google device handoff; it indexes only your files.
facts.setupBlocker: You need an always-on host, ffmpeg, and your own secure remote-access/TLS setup unless you pay a managed host

alternatives.name: Jellyfin
alternatives.desc: A media server that also handles music, because apparently your albums can live beside your films.

facts.install: Native server package for Windows/macOS/Linux/NAS, or Docker/Podman
facts.dataFormat: Media stays in mounted filesystem folders; Jellyfin stores settings, users and indexed metadata in its local server data directory, including a SQLite database
facts.gapVsPaid: It serves owned audio but has none of YouTube Music's enormous video, remix and live-performance catalogue or recommendation system, and its music UI is less specialized.
facts.setupBlocker: You must keep a server running, map media and config storage correctly, and configure networking/TLS for access outside the home

alternatives.name: Koel
alternatives.desc: A clean personal jukebox; solo listening is free, team features are not.

facts.install: Download and extract the standalone Koel/FrankenPHP archive, then run the bundled server; Docker is also available
facts.dataFormat: Music stays at the configured media path; the standalone build keeps configuration, a SQLite database, logs, cache, images and transcodes under ~/.koel/
facts.gapVsPaid: It replaces a personal upload locker, not YouTube Music's licensed and user-uploaded video catalogue, recommendation engine, radio, or Google ecosystem continuity.
facts.setupBlocker: The macOS standalone binary is not code-signed and needs its quarantine flag removed; public access still needs a stable host and domain/reverse-proxy setup

alternatives.name: mStream
alternatives.desc: The small, installable music server for people who do not want a media empire.

facts.install: Prebuilt Windows/macOS/Linux server binary or Docker image
facts.dataFormat: Audio stays in folders on the host; mStream keeps its server configuration, index and generated caches in local application directories or mapped Docker volumes
facts.gapVsPaid: It streams your files but loses YouTube Music's licensed catalogue, rare video and live versions, personalized radio, and broad casting/device integration.
facts.setupBlocker: Browser access away from home still requires DNS, TLS and port forwarding; the easier Quick Sync path currently works only with its native clients

alternatives.name: Swing Music
alternatives.desc: A prettier private jukebox with daily mixes; remote access still becomes your networking hobby.

facts.install: One-line Linux/macOS shell installer, Windows portable build, or Docker Compose
facts.dataFormat: Audio remains in the mounted music directory; Swing Music writes its configuration and indexed library data to a separate local config directory
facts.gapVsPaid: Its local mixes cannot reproduce YouTube Music's licensed video/audio catalogue or recommendation graph, and remote access is your networking responsibility.
facts.setupBlocker: The local installer is easy, but secure listening outside your LAN still means exposing and protecting a web service yourself

alternatives.name: Ampache
alternatives.desc: A mature web jukebox with enough knobs to remind you it predates subscription fatigue.

facts.install: Docker image followed by a browser-based installer, or a PHP web stack with MySQL/MariaDB
facts.dataFormat: Audio/video files remain in server-side catalog folders; users, playlists and indexed metadata live in a MySQL/MariaDB database with a PHP configuration file
facts.gapVsPaid: It has no YouTube catalogue, videos, remixes, recommendations, or Google-device integration, and its older interface is far less effortless for casual listening.
facts.setupBlocker: The first-run wizard asks for database-admin credentials and writable config/catalog paths, so permissions and MySQL setup arrive before music playback

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Individual plan and a personal library or creator utility DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for YouTube Music Premium in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, ffmpeg, and a local web interface; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: organize and stream legally owned or user-created audio, analyze local files, and provide a private playback workflow without accessing YouTube's licensed catalog.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Index only user-selected folders and preserve source audio without modification.
Read tags and artwork, calculate loudness and waveform data, and detect exact duplicates by hash.
Provide albums, artists, playlists, search, queue, favorites, and resumable local playback.
Add optional creator tools for trim, normalize, split stems through a local model, and export new files.
Keep all rights and source information attached to imported tracks and display it during export.
Document that the application does not provide music, licensing, distribution, or royalty collection.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out copyrighted catalog acquisition or sharing.
Deliberately leave out streaming-service circumvention.
Deliberately leave out royalty accounting, label distribution, and global content delivery.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
